ios.desc:
Most app blockers fail for the same reason: they trust you to stop yourself.

But research shows people are significantly more likely to break a habit when someone else is involved. Disconnect App is built on that insight. You set the rules. A trusted person holds the key. When you try to unblock a blocked app, they decide — not you.

No bypass. No weak moments. Just a system that works when willpower doesn't.

HOW IT WORKS

Choose the apps you want to block and when. Then pick your lock level:

Soft Lock — unblock instantly, but tap through a confirmation first. Enough friction to break the reflex.
Medium Lock — wait 5 minutes before access is granted. Enough time to actually reconsider.
Hard Lock — you cannot unblock it yourself. Your buddy gets a notification and decides whether to let you in. No workarounds. No escape hatch.

THE BUDDY SYSTEM

This is what makes Disconnect App different from every other screen time blocker.

You choose someone you trust — a friend, a partner, anyone. When you try to open a hard-locked app, they receive a notification and approve or deny in seconds. It's not surveillance. It's accountability. One person who steps in when your willpower gives out.

Your buddy never sees which apps you use or how long you spend on them. They simply get asked: yes or no?

WHAT'S FREE

· 1 rule
· 1 buddy
· All three lock levels including hard lock
· No time limit — it's yours to keep

DISCONNECT PRO

· Unlimited rules
· Multiple buddies
· More features coming

PRIVACY & LEGAL

Disconnect App uses Apple's Screen Time API. The apps you choose to block never leave your device — we never see them. Only the minimum data needed to run the buddy system is stored: your display name, buddy relationships, and unlock requests. We do not sell your data.

Privacy Policy: https://disconnectapp.co/privacy
Terms of Service: https://disconnectapp.co/terms

quotes.text:
Disconnect is an app blocker for iOS that lets you put a friend in control of granting you access to blocked apps.

Like many, I've personally struggled a lot with phone and social media addiction over the years. I tried the usual tactics to get over this addiction -- deleting the apps (they make their way back in somehow), deactivating my accounts (they get reactivated again somehow), even tried some existing screen time blocking apps as well. Nothing worked. The final thing that worked for me was the following:

1- I changed my passwords to something random, on all the social media apps I wanted to get rid of. Didn't note down these passwords anywhere.

2- Changed the password recovery routes for these accounts to email and phone number of my partner's. Gave them the explicit instruction not to hand over the reset code when I ask, unless I've a compelling reason.

3- Signed out completely.

The above worked surprisingly well. Knowing I can't access the apps myself and have to go through convincing my partner to let me back in, was a significant hurdle to get over.

Disconnect embodies the same mechanism. It lets you pair up with a friend. When you put a hard block on apps, you can only get access to them if your buddy grants you access. You can send an access request from within the Disconnect app.

The app uses system Screen Time APIs on iOS, and all your app usage analytics stays on your device. Your buddy doesn't get any analytics either, beyond the name of the block …
